details: Bitcoin briefly fell below the $80,000 mark on Saturday, reaching its lowest price in over a month. The drop coincided with reports of the United States evacuating personnel from Middle East outposts due to concerns about potential attacks from Iran. This market movement led to $404 million in crypto long positions being liquidated within four hours as broader crypto prices declined.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $80K Amid Geopolitical Tensions & Long Liquidations

details: Wells Fargo, Intuit, and several other major American companies have formally objected to plans by cryptocurrency exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) to list tokenized versions of publicly traded equities. These objections, totaling 22 firms, highlight growing corporate resistance to blockchain-based stock trading initiatives that aim for 24/7 accessibility.
title: Wells Fargo, Intuit Among Firms Objecting to OKX-ICE Tokenized Stock Plans

details: The Initia network was temporarily halted following a security incident where an attacker reportedly minted unauthorized tokens, draining over $2.6 million. This exploit raises concerns about the security of decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols and cross-chain operations.
title: Initia Network Halted After Reported Security Incident

details: A US Senator is reportedly seeking answers from stablecoin issuer Tether regarding a deal with a firm founded by a former White House crypto adviser under the Trump administration. This inquiry signals increasing regulatory scrutiny on stablecoin operations and potential political influence within the crypto sector.
title: US Senator Probes Tether Over Deal with Ex-Trump Crypto Adviser

details: Spot Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) experienced significant net outflows, totaling $636 million, which effectively erased the inflows from the preceding day. This reversal in institutional sentiment suggests a fluctuating interest in Bitcoin ETFs and could indicate broader market caution.
title: Bitcoin ETFs See $636M Outflows, Erasing Previous Day's Inflows
